Take Leadership tests for units with Battleshock tokens (2D6 ≤ Ld to pass). Pass: remove all tokens. Fail: tokens remain. 2 tokens = Fleeing.

Reinforcement Phase

You may roll reinforcement dice equal to the battle round number. Each 4+ must bring one unit from reserve, if possible. They enter from your board edge during their activation in the following Command phase, with an Advance or Move & Shoot order only.

Command Phase

Both players assign orders face-down to all units simultaneously. Orders determine what a unit can do in the Action Phase. All allowed actions of an order must be resolved in the order they are written.

At the end of each Command Phase the player with fewer Orders gets 1 Skip token per 2 Orders of difference, rounded up (1–2 = 1 token, 3–4 = 2, 5–6 = 3). Unused Skip tokens expire at the end of the battle round.
Initiative Phase
Both players roll 2D6. Higher result wins initiative and activates first in the Action Phase. Ties: player who did NOT have initiative last round wins. First round: whoever finished deploying first.
Action Phase
Players alternate activating one unit at a time, starting with the initiative holder. Each unit carries out its assigned order.
A unit may move, shoot, and fight in the same round — but each action only once. A unit already activated may still fight if charged later.

Doing nothing: a unit does not need to perform every part of an order — a Move & Shoot unit may skip either the move or the shooting. Passing: a player with no units left to activate passes, and the other keeps activating until every unit has acted.
Orders
Move up to M. May Advance D6″ extra. Declare any number of visible enemy units as ranged targets — they may answer with Take Cover. Shoot Assault/Pistol/Grenade at −1. Cast basic psychic powers.

With nothing of yours left, they lose their order, count as activated and may only consolidate.

Meta Orders (Defensive Reactions)

Not assigned in the Command Phase — triggered. A Defensive Reaction may only be used by a unit that has not yet been activated this round, and using one removes that unit’s order. None of them can be used by a unit engaged in melee.

Triggered in specific situations — not assigned in the Command Phase. Can only be used by units that haven't activated yet this round and are not in melee. If several units use Defensive Reactions, all declare them simultaneously.
Acute Senses

Requires the Acute Senses ability, a unit that has not activated yet, and an enemy unit deployed from reserves within 12″: fire at it as if it had a Stand & Shoot order. Resolves after the enemy is deployed and before it takes another action.
Counter-Attack
Requires Counter-Attack ability. When declared as a charge target: treated as having executed a Charge order. Must pick Charge bonus before attacker does.
Defensive Fire
When declared as a charge target: fire ranged weapons at the charger at −1 to hit. Attacker auto-passes Leadership during this.
Hold Your Ground
When declared as a charge target: negates the attacker's Charge bonus. At least 50% of charged units must use this to negate the bonus.
Take Cover
When declared as a ranged target: +1 to Saving throws vs ranged attacks and −1 AT (to a minimum of 0) until end of enemy activation.
Unit Formation
In formation
At the end of its movement a unit must be in formation: no model may be more than 2″ horizontally or 5″ vertically from another model in the same unit.
In melee

Units engaged in close combat do not need to maintain formation. After leaving melee,

Enemy models
Models must keep a minimum distance of 1″ from all enemy models. Creatures may move through friendly models; vehicles must be bypassed.
Mixed movement profiles

A unit with models of different movement limits applies them to the whole unit. A character in Terminator armor joining an Infantry unit means the unit cannot Advance and cannot pursue in melee (Unyielding).

Ranged Combat Sequence
Choose Targets — Select targets for all weapons before resolving. At least one model visible and in range. Can't target units in melee.
Resolve Attacks — If multiple targets, resolve all attacks vs one unit before moving to next.
Hit Rolls — Roll to hit vs model's BS. Roll of 6 always succeeds.
Wound Rolls — Roll based on weapon Strength vs target Toughness.

Saving Throws — Roll save, subtract weapon AP. Ward save unaffected by AP. If the required save would be worse than 6+ and the model has no Ward save (or its Ward save is also worse than 6+), skip the roll and apply the damage.

Damage — Failed save = damage equal to weapon profile. When damage ≥ Wounds, model removed. Damage doesn't carry over. Removing casualties ends immediately once no enemy model is left within LOS or within the weapon's range.
Leadership Test — If unit drops below half starting strength, pass Ld test or receive 2 Battleshock tokens.
Line of Sight
At least one model in the target unit must be visible to the attacker. What actually counts as "the model" differs between creatures and vehicles.

Combat Result — Only scored if enemy units are still in base contact; otherwise the remaining side automatically wins. Score: +1 for more remaining wounds, +1 per wound caused (Creatures), +1 per penetrating hit (Vehicles). Winner = more points.
Losing Combat — Loser takes Ld test with penalty = result difference. Fail: 2 Battleshock tokens (flee).
Pursuit — Winner may pursue fleeing units: roll D6+highest I. Match or exceed fleeing unit's roll to catch (+1 auto hit per model, −1 Battleshock token from fleeing unit).

Terrain Types
Normal Terrain
No movement restrictions.
Difficult Terrain
Movement penalty: M3″=−1″ / M6″=−2″ / M12″=−4″ / M24″=−8″ (or 33% rounded up). Penalty applies once per activation. Alt: move full speed but treat as dangerous.
Dangerous Terrain
Each model rolls 1D6; each 1 = wound (no saves). Vehicles suffer Engine Damage instead. Test once per activation.
Impassable Terrain
Cannot pass through. Anti-Grav and Jump Pack models may move over it. Cannot end movement on it.
Melee over Terrain
Two units separated by a terrain piece — a sandbag barrier, a wall — can still fight each other, but only if all three of these are true:
At least one model among the two units is 33% taller than the terrain piece between them.
The terrain piece separates the two units by no more than 1″.
The terrain piece has no roof at all, or a crevice/window between them at least 0.5″ tall and wide.
Miss any one of the three and there is no melee over that terrain piece.

Vehicle Destruction
A vehicle is destroyed when it loses its last Hull Point, and how it lost it decides what happens next.
Wreckage

Last Hull Point lost to Engine, Weapon or Structural Damage. The model stays on the table as difficult terrain. Passengers disembark within 3″ and each must pass a Leadership test or take a Battleshock token.
Explosion

Last Hull Point lost to Critical Damage. Every model within D6″ takes a S5 / AP 0 / D1 hit. Passengers take those wounds automatically and get a Battleshock token. Casualties count towards the combat result in melee. Survivors disembark within 3″ and act on their activation according to how far the vehicle had moved.
Emergency Disembarkation

If passengers cannot be placed — terrain or enemies in the way — they disembark within 6″ instead but count as activated for the rest of the round. Models that still cannot be placed are removed from play.
Flyers: passengers may only disembark in Hover mode, and an exploding flyer deals them double the automatic wounds.
Mixed Units
Mixed Armour Save: Use the save value that occurs most. Tie = controlling player chooses. Casualties from failed saves must come from models matching that save first.
Mixed Toughness: Use the T value that occurs most. Tie = controlling player chooses.
Mixed Defensive Rules: Use the special rule (or lack of one) that occurs most.
Characters: Cannot voluntarily take wounds for the unit. Always use their own armour/invul save.
Suppressive Fire

A unit scoring 6+ ranged hits in its activation forces the target to take a Ld test. For every additional 6 hits: cumulative −1 penalty. Fail → 1 Battleshock token (if they had none). If the target would also have to test for dropping below half Starting Strength at the same time, it rolls only for Suppressive Fire — and a failure gives 2 tokens even if it already had one.

Transports
Embarking: a unit within 3″ at the end of its movement can board a transport. Passengers cannot be given a Stand & Shoot order. Any number of units may ride, up to the vehicle’s transport capacity.
What the passengers may do depends on how far the transport moved this activation:

Use fire hatches or disembark within 3″. Execute their command normally.
>0″–6″
Use fire hatches or disembark within 3″. Execute their command. Cannot move or Charge.

Use fire hatches or disembark within 3″. Execute their command at −1 to hit until the end of the battle round. Cannot move or Charge.

Fire Hatches: each one lets a single passenger fire their weapon when the unit activates. A vehicle with the Open rule has fire hatches equal to its passenger capacity — and its passengers can be shot at, count as physically on the battlefield for ranges and psychic powers (measured from the hull), share the transport’s cover, cannot fight in melee from inside, and can always make a 6″ Charge move after disembarking if the vehicle moved up to 12″.
A transport and the units inside it count as one reserve: a single 4+ brings them on together. For what happens when the transport is destroyed, see Vehicle Destruction under Combat.
Profile Values Reference
Movement — Speed in inches. "−" = cannot move.
Weapon Skill — Melee hit roll target. "−" = cannot fight in melee. Max 1+.
Ballistic Skill — Ranged hit roll target. "−" = cannot shoot. Max 1+.
Strength — Melee wounding power. Max 10 or D.
Toughness — Damage resistance. Max 10.
Wounds — Damage capacity. Excess damage doesn't carry over between models.
Initiative — Melee activation order, highest first. Max 10.
Attacks — Melee attacks per activation. "−" = cannot fight in melee. Max 10.
Leadership — Bravery. Uses highest in squad including attached characters. Max 10.
Save — Armour protection, modified by weapon AP. Roll of 1 always fails. Max 1+.
Ward Save — Not affected by AP. Max 4+ (unless stated otherwise).
Modifying Profile Values
Order of modifications — additive first (+1), then multiplicative (×2), then subtractive (−1). The order matters: the same three modifiers applied in another order give a different number.

Modifying Strength: if a model’s Strength changes, it gains a temporary minimum AT value in melee unless it is already as good or better. At Strength 7 or higher all its melee attacks have AT(1), again unless already better.
Profile Value Tests

Some rules call for a test against a profile value — a “Toughness test”, a “Leadership value test”. Roll 1D6. The roll must be equal to or below the value to pass, and a roll of 6 always fails. Use the current value, after any equipment, psychic power or other modifier.

Not the same thing as the Leadership test for Battleshock, which is 2D6 against Leadership. The opposite convention applies to attacks: on a hit or wound roll a 6 always succeeds whatever the target number, while an armour save of 1 always fails.
Weapon Profile Reference
Range — Maximum distance in inches, measured from the model's base (or, lacking one, any part of the hull). A “−” means melee only.
Type — Assault, Grenade, Heavy, Melee, Pistol or Rapid Fire. Ranged weapons only shoot and Melee weapons only fight, unless stated otherwise.
Strength — 1–10, or D for a Destroyer weapon. U means the wielder's own Strength; a modifier (“+1”, “x2”) applies to it.
Armor Piercing — How far it reduces the target's armour save. AP −3 is better than AP −1; AP 0 applies no modifier.
Damage — Damage inflicted by a successful attack, after failed saves.
Abilities — Special rules for the weapon; see the Weapon Abilities section below, the Codex, or the army list entry.

Deep Strike

Models arriving from reserve via Deep Strike can be placed anywhere on the battlefield. They are only allowed to receive the "Charge" or "Move & Shoot" order. Deployment Process: Place one model from the unit on the battlefield in the desired position. Roll a scatter die: If the result is a hit icon, the model remains in place. If the result is an arrow, move the model 2D6" in the indicated direction. Remaining models in the unit must be placed in a circle around the first model, touching it. If the first circle is full, begin a second circle, with each model touching one from the first circle. If the first model lands outside the playing field, on impassable terrain or another unit, the unit goes back into reserve and must take a dangerous terrain test. Models placed on terrain must take a dangerous terrain test, even if they normally ignore terrain. Placement Exceptions: If models cannot be placed due to space limitations, they count as destroyed. On terrain floors, models are only destroyed if there is no more available space. Empty spaces in the circle can be mentally skipped. The unit counts as having moved 6" and can't move any further with its regular Movement profile. The unit may still make its "Charge move". The unit may only perform a "Disorderly Charge".

Auto Hit

Beam

Choose a target and make a hit roll with the weapon as normal. If the hit is successful, draw a 1mm straight line from the nearest point of the shooting model's base to the nearest point of a model in the target unit. Make a wound roll against the target unit and any other units the line passes over.
Blast (X)

A successful hit roll with this weapon generates 1 hit per model in the target unit, to a maximum of X hits. An unsuccessful hit roll can be re-rolled once and can only generate half (rounded down) that many maximum hits.
Blind
If a weapon with this rule scores at least one hit, the target unit may only perform a Disorderly Charge.
Blood Drinker
For each Wound loss the model causes, it regains 1 Wound, up to the starting value in its profile. Example: A weapon with Damage 2 killing a unit with 1 Wound would restore 1 Wound.
Bomb
The range of this weapon is unaffected by the range reduction rules for Flyers.
A weapon profile with this ability can only be used if the model is using a Charge command (even if making a Disorderly Charge).
Combi
Combination weapons, like the "Combi-melta," combine two profiles into one. A combi-weapon can fire both profiles simultaneously at the same target, with a -1 penalty to hit.
Deadly (X)
Successful wound rolls of X+ increase the Damage value of the attack by +1.
Decimate
Wound rolls gain a +1 bonus. Does not work against Vehicles.
Deflagrate (X)
Successful hit rolls of X+ score an additional hit. Does not work with Blast(x) weapons.
Extra Attack (X)

A ranged weapon can be used X times with its profile during each activation, in addition to the model's normal shooting attacks. A melee weapon makes X attacks with its profile during each activation, in addition to the model's normal Attacks (A). A model may only benefit from extra attacks from one Armoury weapon.
Force Weapon
If the bearer successfully manifests at least one psychic power during their activation, any Force weapon they carry gains +1 Damage for the remainder of the battle round.
Grav
Unless it would already be better, the wound roll equals the enemy unit's armor save. Unless already worse, the armor save against this weapon is always 5+. Does not work against Vehicles.
Graviton

Creatures that lose a wound by this weapon must pass a Strength test or suffer another wound with S: 4 AP: 0 D: 1; Seeking. This is in addition to the actual wound roll. If the target enemy unit is in cover and at least one hit is scored with this weapon, the terrain becomes difficult and dangerous terrain until the next unit activation that caused the hit.
Gruesome
Every wound caused by a weapon with this rule counts as two for combat resolution. Models that are caught while fleeing from close combat suffer an additional automatic wound from this weapon.
Haywire
Each hit causes one automatic penetrating hit against a Vehicle, in addition to any normal damage. Does not work against Creatures.
Hover Mode
The model is eligible to use the "Stand & Shoot" order to land.
Indirect

The weapon can target enemy units and cause casualties without LOS. Targets only gain a cover bonus if they are in a terrain zone. Weapons can only be fired indirectly using the "Stand & Shoot" command.
Life Curse

A single wound roll can be re-rolled against Creatures. If multiple models in a unit have the same weapon with this rule, they can make their wound rolls together. In this case, one wound roll per model may be re-rolled.
Limit (X)
Only X attacks can be made with this weapon each turn.
Master-crafted

A single hit roll can be re-rolled. If the weapon has the "Blast(x)" or "Auto Hit" ability, a single wound or armor penetration roll can be re-rolled instead. If multiple models in a unit have the same weapon with this rule, the corresponding hit rolls can be made together. In this case, one hit roll per model may be re-rolled. Can't be used on "Grenade" type weapons or weapons with the "Ammo(x)" ability.
Melta
When targeting units within half the weapon's maximum range, the weapon gains +1 Damage, +2 AT and gains a +3 bonus for armor penetration.
Monofilament
If at least one hit has been scored with the weapon, the target counts as being in difficult and dangerous terrain until the end of the next activation of the target unit.
Overheating

Self-Inflicted Damage on Hit Rolls: Each roll of a 1 on a hit roll with this weapon causes the user to suffer a Mortal Wound. If the model is a vehicle, it instead suffers a glancing hit using the weapon's AT value. Re-Roll Restriction: If the model has any ability to re-roll hit rolls (such as from Blast(x), Psychic effects, or other rules), the result of the initial roll determines whether the weapon is overheating. Automatic Hits: For weapons that hit automatically, any roll of a 1 when determining wound rolls causes the user to suffer the same penalty: a Mortal Wound or, for vehicles, a glancing hit using the weapon's AT value. Wound Assignment: Wounds caused by Overheating must be allocated first to models equipped with Overheating weapons. These wounds cannot spill over to other models without Overheating weapons, overriding the standard rule that entire models must be removed first.
Piercing (X)

Successful wound rolls of X+ always succeed and gain an additional -2 AP. Successful armor penetration rolls of X+ gain a +2 bonus to the result and are considered to have AT(1) unless their AT is already higher.
Poison (X)
Wound rolls of X+ against creatures always succeed. Can be affected by effects that give bonuses or penalties to wound rolls.
Precision (X)
Successful hit rolls of X+ automatically wound creatures. Can't be used with "Blast(x)" weapons.
Psi-shock

If a creature unit gets hit, a randomly chosen psyker model in that unit must pass a Leadership value test or suffer 1D3 Mortal Wounds. If a vehicle unit gets hit, a randomly chosen psyker model in that unit must pass a Leadership value test or suffer 1D3 instances of Critical Damage. Each additional hit from the same unit during the same activation incurs a cumulative -1 penalty for the test. Can't be triggered more than once per activated unit.
Quick (X)
The model gains X to its Initiative.
Rad
A unit hit by this weapon suffers a -1 penalty to its Toughness value until the end of its next activation.
Rending (X)
Successful wound rolls of X+ gain an additional bonus of -1 to their AP.
Seeking
Enemy units in cover do not gain any cover benefit against this weapon and are treated as being outside of cover.
Shield Breaker (X)
Ward saves of enemy models are degraded by X.
Shred
The model may re-roll any wound rolls made with this weapon. Does not work against Vehicles.
Slow (X)
The model suffers X to its Initiative.
Sniper

The model gains +1 Ballistic Skill when using a weapon with this ability. The model may select a specific character model in the target unit for all to hit and to wound rolls. Use the target's individual defensive profile for hitting and wounding it. Models with the Bodyguard ability must be targeted first, before a character model may be selected.
Soul Burn (X)

Successful wound rolls of X+ against Creatures inflict 1 Mortal Wound in addition to any normal weapon damage, even if the wound gets saved. Does not work against Vehicles. Excess wounds do not spill over to the next model, as the Mortal Wound is part of the original attack.
Sunder (X)
Enemy units in cover reduce the benefit to their armor save from cover by -X (to a minimum of 0).
Suppression (X)
Every hit from a weapon with this ability counts as X hits when determining Suppressive Fire.
Unwieldy
The model does not gain an additional attack for having a pistol in close combat.

Alliance Levels
Battle Brothers
Allied units are treated as friendly in all respects.
Auras and psychic powers can be cast on allied units.
Transport vehicles can carry units from both factions freely.
Allies of Convenience
Allied units are treated as separate armies.
Auras and psychic powers only affect the primary faction's units.
Transports can only carry units of the primary faction.
Desperate Allies
Same restrictions as Allies of Convenience, plus:
Units within 12″ of the ally must pass a Ld test (−1) or lose their order for that turn.
Uses own mini-AOP: 0–1 HQ · 1–2 Troops · 0–1 Elite/FA/HS per Troop · 0–ᵀ Transports.
Cannot select a second AOP after filling all slots.
May select own Army Customisation options.
A faction may always ally with itself. Two Inquisition forces or two Dark Eldar Kabals allied together count as Allies of Convenience (Y), not Battle Brothers.

* For each Troop unit, one Elite, Fast Attack, or Heavy Support unit may be chosen.
Allies cannot select a second AOP after filling all available slots.
Allies may select their own Army Customisation options.
Allying with the same faction: a faction may ally with itself. Both parts are considered one army, so "Unique" equipment or "once per army" upgrades (like HQ selections) can still only be taken once.
Limitation: units in an allied detachment can never make use of the "Objective secured!" rule.
Setting Up Units
Both players compare their total unit count. For every 2-unit difference, the player with fewer units receives a pass marker.

Deployment sequence: the player who won the side pick begins. Starting with them, players alternate placing one unit (with any attached characters) in their deployment zone. Instead of placing a unit, a player may:
Board a transport: announce a unit is embarking and place the transport with any units (including attached characters).
Start in reserve: the unit enters the battlefield later.
Character joins a reserve unit: announce a character joins a unit held in reserve.
Infiltration: the unit is set up as an infiltrator and placed later.
Character joins an infiltrator unit: announce a character joins a unit as infiltrators.
Fortification setup: remove a piece of terrain at least 50% within your deployment zone and replace it with a Fortification-type unit.
Pass marker: skip a unit placement. After using a pass marker once, the player must deploy a unit next.

Infiltrators are placed alternately, the same way as normal units, after all other units are deployed. They do not count when determining the initiative bonus for the game. Some missions may outrule reserve or infiltrator options — always check the mission first.
Playing Your First Game
Game size: 2500 points per player.
Table size: 72″ × 48″.
Mission: Take & Hold.
Skip the Army Customisation options at first — use the datasheets as written.
Go easy on vehicle use for both sides.
For a smaller game, use the Skirmish rules in the Mission Supplement (with unit limitations to keep it balanced).
It is strongly recommended to use the Mission Supplement — the game is balanced around objective-based play.
Casting Psychic Powers
Models with the Psyker rule can manifest psychic powers.
Powers are classified as Basic, Normal, or Complex — see each order for which categories can be cast.
Roll 2D6. Result must meet or exceed the power's cast value.
Casting the same power again in the same turn: −1 cumulative penalty per attempt.
Requires LOS to target unless stated otherwise.
Psykers have access to the General Disciplines and their Codex disciplines.
Overchanneling
May roll an extra die (3D6 total) when manifesting a power. Suffers D3 Mortal Wounds on any double (in addition to any Perils of the Warp).
Dispelling
Some models may dispel powers. If an enemy psyker within 24″ successfully manifests a power: roll 2D6. Result must be greater than the psychic test result to dispel. Dispelled powers have no effect.
Psychic Powers in Melee
Psykers in melee can only cast basic psychic powers during their initiative phase.
Targets limited to: the psyker, or friendly/enemy units in the same melee.
Psykers not in melee cannot target units in melee with Witchfire powers.
Hymns, Invocations & Prayers
Cannot be dispelled. May only be attempted once per battle round per unit. If the user is eliminated, effects persist until the Rally phase of the next battle round.
Perils of the Warp
Triggered on a double 1 or double 6 during the psychic test. Roll 1D6:
Name
Sucked into the Warp
Pass Ld value test: 1 Mortal Wound. Fail: removed as casualty.
Mindsteal
1 Mortal Wound. The attempted power cannot be used for the rest of the game.
Power Drain
1 Mortal Wound. Roll 1D3: both players subtract result from all psychic tests for the rest of the round (cumulative).
Psionic Feedback
1 Mortal Wound.
Empyrian Aftermath
Fail Ld value test: 1 Mortal Wound.
Warp Boost
Pass Ld value test: +1 to hit and +1 to wound rolls until end of next activation. Fail: 1 Mortal Wound.
Vehicles use Leadership 10 for Perils tests. Fearless models still must pass Leadership value tests.
